answer.sameness: The set resolves into a handful of repeated families: dark automotive photo heroes with uppercase headlines and registration-plate phone numbers; cream bordered text cards overlapping restaurant photographs; teal framed cards with circular retail/florist imagery; and salon heroes with oversized pale lettering and arched photographs. Many regenerated pages converge on the same white, rectangular-photo-and-text split, then stack photograph above copy on mobile. Typography repeatedly alternates between heavy compact sans-serif and editorial serif, with burgundy, teal, mustard or brown accents. Three hospitality businesses share the same building photograph, and several automotive businesses use
recurringIssues: Identical hero photographs across different businesses make supposedly individual identities visibly interchangeable.
Many regenerated pages lose distinctive composition and become the same restrained photo-and-text template.
Some hero photographs do not communicate the service: mountain scenery fronts both joinery and tyre servicing.
Several desktop layouts leave substantial white space around undersized copy and weak calls to action.
Mobile headers and bottom action bars repeatedly duplicate contact controls, consuming space without strengthening the hierarchy.
Decorative frames, arches, oversized background lettering and phone-number plates recur as template signatures rather than business-specific ideas.

best.why: The warm dark palette, substantial bread photography, arched crop and circular opening-time badge form one of the most cohesive and recognisable identities across both sizes.
Fresh mint colouring, confident headline hierarchy and an asymmetric treatment-room composition give the practice a calm but distinctive presence.
Strong serif typography and paired arched photographs create a considered editorial identity that remains recognisable on mobile.

weakest.why: The mountain backdrop fails to establish tyre servicing, while the dark overlay, uppercase headline and phone-number plate reproduce the automotive template almost unchanged.
A landscape photograph occupies the main opportunity to show craftsmanship, leaving an otherwise sparse layout with little visual evidence of joinery.
The small desktop headline, narrow contact column and largely unarticulated white space make the page feel like a generic information sheet rather than a designed business identity.

answer.oneChange: Require a distinct, business-specific hero concept for every homepage, built around relevant imagery and its own composition rather than selecting another variant of the same layout family.
answer.summary: This is competent template production, not yet a distinctive studio portfolio. Most pages have readable hierarchy and sensible mobile stacking, and a few show genuine visual character. However, repeated photographs, recognisable layout families and near-identical contact treatments make unrelated businesses look interchangeable. The regenerated pages often improve restraint but flatten identity into the same white photo-and-copy arrangement. Invest first in business-specific imagery and hero concepts; another palette or font swap will not solve the sameness.
